Name of the Surah

• It is called al-Takathur (Rivalry in Worldly Gain), because it opens with the preoccupation of people with takathur, which is boasting of the abundance of wealth and children.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• Rebuking people for their heedlessness of the Hereafter and their preference for this world, and their failure to desist from this until they end up in the graves; and warning and threatening them over that heedlessness by reminding them of the punishment in the Hereafter and of the reckoning that will follow for neglecting to thank the Great Bestower.

[The Tafsir]

﴿The rivalry in worldly gain diverted you﴾ from obedience to God, the boasting of the abundance of wealth and children.

The commentary on 102:2 (﴿حَتَّىٰ زُرْتُمُ الْمَقَابِرَ﴾, "until you visit the graves"):

Your preoccupation with that continued until you came to the graves and were buried in them.
Not thus should the pursuit of abundance in wealth distract you. You will soon come to know that the Hereafter is better for you.
Then beware! You will soon come to know the evil consequence of your being preoccupied with it.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 102, verses 5–8:

This is not how it should be: that abundance in wealth should distract you. If you knew with true knowledge, you would be restrained and would hasten to save yourselves from destruction. You will surely see the Hellfire, then you will surely see it with certainty, and then you will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about every kind of delight.
